what: Dick's Sporting Goods is America's largest sporting goods retailer, selling athletic clothing, footwear and equipment through about 850 stores, and it bought Foot Locker in 2025.
customers: American families buying sports equipment, and sneaker buyers through the Foot Locker chain.
money: sporting goods, athletic apparel and footwear
House of Sport and specialty formats
large experiential stores and Golf Galaxy
moat: Being the last national sporting goods chain standing after competitors failed, which gives it the shelf space the big athletic brands need in America.
risks: $5.8B of debt after the Foot Locker purchase
Foot Locker was losing share before the deal and turning it round is unproven
Nike and other brands keep selling more directly to consumers, bypassing retailers
opportunities: 14.8 times earnings with revenue up from $12.3B to $17.2B
The House of Sport format produces far higher sales per square foot than ordinary stores
Analysts see about 16% upside, with 24 covering the stock
watch: Comparable sales at Dick's separately from Foot Locker, and the integration costs.
